root_idea.summary: The root centers on opening, cleaving, or breaking through something.
root_idea.development: From the opening of darkness into dawn and the opening of channels so water flows, the root develops meanings of bursting forth and causing flow. Figuratively, departure from the straight way becomes sinful transgression, while a further classical branch concerns overflowing generosity.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural active participle فُجَّار is presented under the supported singular dictionary citation form فَاجِر.

senses.definition: To break open or open a passage so that water gushes or flows forth.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, used transitively of causing a spring or water source to gush forth.

senses.definition: To persist in sinful defiance or denial, departing from the way of truth.
senses.usage_conditions: In 75:5, the expression concerns continuing in wrongdoing or denying what lies ahead, including resurrection and judgment, while postponing repentance.

senses.definition: To cause water to gush forth by opening or making channels, springs, or sources.
senses.usage_conditions: The intensive/causative Form II is used of making water flow abundantly; the Quran also has a passive use meaning that waters are made to gush forth.

senses.definition: To burst open and gush or flow forth.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive or quasi-reflexive development of opening, used in the Quran of springs or water bursting forth.

senses.definition: To burst open and gush or flow forth.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quran of water bursting from a source and flowing out.

senses.definition: A wicked or transgressing person; one who departs from obedience and the way of truth.
senses.usage_conditions: The singular فَاجِر and the Quranic plural فُجَّار/فَجَرَةُ function as active-participial descriptions of persistently sinful people.

senses.definition: Daybreak; the light that breaks through the darkness before sunrise.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic noun includes the dawn whose spreading marks the beginning of the day; classical discussion distinguishes a preliminary false dawn from the true spreading dawn relevant to fasting and prayer.

senses.definition: Wickedness, sinful transgression, or breach of religious obedience.
senses.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the condition or conduct of departing from the bounds of right conduct.

senses.definition: Causing water to gush forth or flow abundantly.
senses.usage_conditions: The Form II verbal noun denotes the act and its abundant or repeated effect, especially the opening of channels or springs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleave, cut, or open something, especially lengthwise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the primary concrete branch from which the water-opening meanings develop.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To open a vent or passage for a fluid to flow forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classically applied to water, blood, and other fluids; the Quranic water use is listed under the Form I sense above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline, lean, decline, or deviate from a course; also to err in answering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The deviation may be literal, as of a rider from a saddle, or figurative, as from a proper course or answer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lie or commit a foul act, such as swearing a false oath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a classical moral and forensic use related to departure from the right course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To disobey or oppose someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This transitive construction is distinct from the intransitive description of being sinful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perform an action that induces doubt, suspicion, or an evil opinion.
To commit adultery or fornication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may take a partner with بِـ; the meaning is a classical specialization of sinful conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pursue a headlong, rash, or random course without regard to its destination.
Of a case or state of affairs, to become bad.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiomatic expression فَجَرَ أَمْرُهُمْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dim or dull in sight.
To become free from an illness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an intransitive idiomatic construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attribute wickedness to someone, or accuse or charge someone with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction takes a person as the object and is comparable to calling that person sinful or transgressive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a spring or source well forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use, distinct from the Quran-attested Form II causative.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a gift large or be generous in giving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a figurative or assumed-tropical extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter upon, or approach, the time of daybreak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in temporal expressions for the onset or approach of dawn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring or possess much property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated abundance of property is termed فَجَرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For water to have a passage opened and pour, run, or stream forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This intransitive Form VII meaning is the broader classical counterpart of the Quranic bursting-water use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come upon people suddenly and in great number, as an enemy or calamity pours upon them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension emphasizing sudden and abundant onset.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be profuse in generosity, bounty, or beneficence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of overflowing or pouring forth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For dawn to break forth, or for night to depart before the rising dawn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical dawn expression, distinct from the Quranic Form VII water occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To forge or invent speech without having heard or learned it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with فِي الْكَلَامِ, ‘in speech.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: The time of daybreak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A temporal metonymy derived from the dawn itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The prayer performed at daybreak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is used metonymically with the prefixed word for prayer omitted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The troubles or hardships of present existence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Donation, generosity, bounty, or munificence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate classical noun branch, sometimes emphasizing large or ample generosity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Property, much property, or abundance of wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Distinct from the generosity meaning, though the two can occur in the same lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proper-name form used in the sense of vice, wickedness, or a foul deed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It occurs in idioms for lying, false swearing, adultery, fornication, or other foul conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The last child born to a woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Roads or ways.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural whose singular is not specified in the cited discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Days of Fijār, conflicts in which Arabs violated the sanctity of the sacred months.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is associated with transgression of what was held sacred and with the expressions فَجَرْنَا and فِجَار.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Arabs’ contests or rivalries in boasting and glorying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural expression referring to competitive acts of boasting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Inclining, leaning, declining, or falling away from the road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial description of deviation from a course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A liar or one who denies a matter; also a false oath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The false-oath expression is a figurative use; the Quranic wicked-person sense is listed under the public form above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An adulterer or fornicator.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical specialization of the active participle for a person committing sexual immorality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An enchanter or practitioner of enchantment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use reported for the active participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having much wealth or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A possessive epithet derived from the separate noun فَجَرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of opening through which water flows, including a channel, outlet, or low ground into which valleys pour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural مَفَاجِرُ may designate the parts of a valley where a torrent disperses or places opened for irrigation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road or way through sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized place noun.

cautions: Form I has separate Quranic water-opening and moral-transgression uses; the latter is specifically tied to the construction in 75:5.

The public فَاجِر entry combines the singular active participle with its Quranic plural فُجَّار under the singular dictionary citation form; the occurrence count remains the sum of the two QAC groups.
